title: Legal opinion
ruleSource: Written from S.A Badmus' Professional Ethics and Skills drafts (Lawdeck knowledge base). To be confirmed by the legal reviewer.

parts.why: The letterhead: the sender's name, address and contacts at the top. Source: Professional Ethics drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

References come before the date; leave them blank if none was given. Letters are dated; notices and resolutions carry their date at the end. Source: Professional Ethics drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
The addressee's name or office and address, before the salutation. Source: Professional Ethics drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
The salutation. A legal opinion is a memo within an organisation, or a letter to a third party. Source: Professional Ethics drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
The subject heading. Source: Professional Ethics drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.instruction: Write the 'Facts' section of a legal opinion from the facts given, beginning 'Sequel to our earlier discussion on ...': a short, neutral statement of the material facts and the documents supplied.
parts.why: States the facts on which the opinion is based. Source: Professional Ethics drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
parts.heading: FACTS

parts.instruction: Write the 'Analysis' section of a legal opinion: identify each legal issue raised by the facts and analyse it against the applicable law, with authorities only from the library passages supplied.
parts.why: Analyses the facts against the law, issue by issue. Source: Professional Ethics drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
parts.heading: ANALYSIS

parts.instruction: Write the 'Opinion' section of a legal opinion: the writer's clear conclusion and recommended course of action, beginning 'Flowing from the foregoing, ...'.
parts.why: The opinion proper: the conclusion and the recommended option. Source: Professional Ethics drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
parts.heading: OPINION

parts.text: This opinion states the position of the law as at the date it is given, and is based on the facts and documents made available to us.
parts.why: The disclaimer: the law as at the date, and the facts and documents supplied. Source: Professional Ethics drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

The complimentary close, the signature space, and the name and capacity of the person signing. Always sign a draft in the exam. Source: Professional Ethics drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

fields.label: Sender
fields.question: Who is the letter from? The law firm, company or person, as it appears on the letterhead.

fields.label: Sender's address and contacts
fields.question: The sender's address, email and phone number for the letterhead.

fields.label: Date of the letter
fields.question: What date should the letter bear? Use a date close to the facts, never after the exam date.

fields.label: Addressee
fields.question: Who is the letter to? Give the name or office, for example The Divisional Police Officer.

fields.label: Capacity of the person signing
fields.question: In what capacity do they sign? For example: Principal Partner, Company Secretary.

changeLog.note: First draft for legal review, from the course drafting materials in the knowledge base.
